Alina: ran the overnight profiler on the canary (route=/chat/execute) — p95 token latency jumped ~40ms after the kernel routing change. looks like the selector picked fast_matmul_v2 for longer sequences and that coincides with a ~12% drop in KV cache hit rate :confused:
Jorge: can you paste the perf trace? which phase is spiking (decode vs validate vs kv lookup)?
Alina: attaching quick excerpt from the trace — token breakdown shows spike in `validation` and a smaller bump in `kv_lookup`. decode stayed flat. trace id=trace-2026-03-17-09
perf-bot: metric snapshot: query=sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_count[5m])) by (route,phase,kernel_choice)
perf-bot: results: route=/chat/execute phase=validation kernel_choice=fast_matmul_v2 p95=95ms (was 55ms before) ; kv_hit_rate=0.78 (was 0.90)
Bo: hmm. validation is our function-call/structured-output validator, right? If kernel changes memory layout it could be affecting our validation hotpaths (extra copies / cache misses). also batching heuristics could be producing larger microbatches that push us into a different kernel path
Sasha: agreed. short-term: we should instrument token-level latency with phase tags (decode/kv/validation/serialize). Dashboards need a per-route KPI panel that shows token-latency breakdown stacked by phase + kernel_choice tag. Also separate panel for kv_cache_hit_rate by route and batch_size distribution
Jorge: repro steps I ran: 1) replay 5k requests with function_call enabled 2) seq_len distribution skewed to 512+ 3) observed router picking fast_matmul_v2 at batch_size>=16
Jorge: log snippet:
```
2026-03-17T09:12:11Z INFO kernel_selector: picked fast_matmul_v2 for model=redwood-7b seq=544 batch=18 reason=throughput
2026-03-17T09:12:11Z DEBUG kvcache: hit=false key=abcd1234 route=/chat/execute
2026-03-17T09:12:11Z INFO validator: function-validate took=88ms request=id=xyz
```
Alina: proposal: 1) add kernel_choice tag to existing latency spans 2) add phase tags at token granularity 3) adjust batching heuristic: if function_call_validation=true then cap microbatch to 12 or prefer kernel=fast_matmul_v1 (lower mem but consistent layout) 4) run 10% canary with new routing metric and observe p95/p99 and kv hit
Bo: +1 on tagging. also instrument number_of_retries for function calls (we saw retries bumping when validator times out and the client resubmits). That explains some extra tokens seen on kv miss sequences
Sasha: I'll make the dashboard changes — new panels: 
- Per-route token latency breakdown (stacked phases) with kernel_choice filter
- Function-call validation latency histogram (p50/p95/p99)
- Retry count by route and by user_id
- KV cache hit-rate heatmap (route x time)
I'll also add an alert: token_validation_latency_p95 > 200ms for 5m
Jorge: can we add a compact PromQL we can paste into the dashboard? e.g. `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,route,phase,kernel_choice))`
Alina: yup, and for kv hit rate: `sum(rate(kvcache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kvcache_requests_total[5m])) by (route)`
perf-bot: deploy-bot created canary build redwood-runtime-canary@2026-03-17-10:15 (10% traffic)
Bo: I'll start a small experiment patch that pins kernel_choice for routes with function_call enabled and also limits microbatching. will open PR with perf numbers. cc @Sasha for dashboards and @Jorge for reproduction notes :thumbsup:
Sasha: thanks — will add links in the PR and create a dashboard row in /dashboards/runtime/perf-canary
Alina: leaving this thread here — next steps: PR from Bo, dashboard row from Sasha, monitor canary for 2 hours then rollback if p99 token tail increases. tagging follow-ups in the canary run ticket.
Jorge: FYI I captured a flamegraph and uploaded to the perf bucket: gs://redwood-perf/traces/trace-2026-03-17-09.flame
Alina: great. will check post-merge. :rocket:
